title: Public transport in Kazakhstan
paragraphs: Kazakhstan is the ninth largest country in the world by area, covering more than 2.7 million square kilometres. Getting around this vast country is an important part of everyday life, and Kazakhstanis use a wide variety of transport options depending on where they live and where they need to go. From modern metro systems in the big cities to long-distance trains crossing the steppe, the transport network of Kazakhstan is fascinating and diverse.

In the biggest cities — Almaty, Astana, and Shymkent — urban transport is well developed. Almaty has the only metro system in Kazakhstan, with two lines and around 10 stations. The metro is fast, clean, and very affordable — a single journey costs only about 100 tenge. However, the metro does not cover the whole city, so many people also use buses, minibuses (called "marshrutkas"), and taxis. Marshrutkas are very popular because they are cheap and go almost everywhere, but they can be crowded and noisy during rush hour.

Buses are the backbone of city transport across Kazakhstan. Every major city has a network of numbered bus routes. In Uralsk — where WKU is located — students use buses daily to travel between the university, the dormitory, the city centre, and the market. A bus fare in Uralsk costs around 80–100 tenge, and you can pay with a transport card or cash. Most buses in large cities now have electronic displays and audio announcements of the next stop, which makes them easy to use even for visitors.

Taxis are extremely convenient in Kazakhstan, especially with the arrival of app-based services like Yandex Go and InDrive. You open the app, type in your destination, see the price before you book, and the driver arrives in just a few minutes. This is much safer and more transparent than hailing a random taxi on the street. Students at WKU use taxi apps regularly — especially late at night or when carrying heavy bags after a shopping trip.

For long-distance travel between cities, Kazakhstanis traditionally use trains. The national railway company is called Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZh). There are direct train routes between all major cities, and ticket prices are reasonable. A journey from Uralsk to Almaty takes about 24 hours by train, or just 2 hours by plane. Trains have different classes: platzkart (open dormitory style, most affordable), kupé (4-person compartments), and first class (called SV — two-person compartments with air conditioning).

Air travel has become increasingly popular in Kazakhstan. The main airline is Air Astana, which flies to all major cities within Kazakhstan and to many international destinations. Low-cost airlines like Fly Arystan offer very affordable domestic flights. Students sometimes fly home for holidays, especially if their city is far from Uralsk. The nearest airport to WKU is Oral Airport, located about 6 kilometres from the city centre. You can get there by taxi in about 15 minutes.

Cycling is becoming more popular in Kazakhstani cities, particularly among young people and students. Many cities have started building dedicated cycling lanes, and bike-sharing schemes have appeared in Almaty and Astana. However, cycling in winter — when temperatures can drop to minus 30 degrees — is not practical! In summer, Kamila and her friends often rent bikes on weekends and cycle along the river embankment, which is one of the most pleasant ways to explore Uralsk.

The most important thing about transport in Kazakhstan is planning ahead. Always check the bus schedule, save the taxi app on your phone, and buy train tickets in advance — they sell out quickly during the holiday season. Whether you are travelling across the city or across the country, Kazakhstan's transport system will get you where you need to go. As Kamila always says: "In Kazakhstan, the distances are big, but so is the adventure!" 🚌✈️🚂

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Amir, how do you usually get to university in the morning?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I take the number 14 bus. It stops right in front of the dormitory. What about you?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I usually walk — it only takes about 20 minutes. But when I'm late, I use Yandex Go.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Taxi apps are so convenient! How much does it usually cost from the dorm to WKU?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: About 400–500 tenge. It's not expensive. Have you ever taken the intercity bus to Aktobe?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Yes, twice. It takes about six hours and costs around 3,000 tenge. Comfortable enough.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I prefer the train. It's slower but I love watching the steppe through the window.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Ha! I prefer to arrive. What's the fastest way to get to Almaty from here?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: By plane — about two hours. Air Astana has three flights a week from Oral Airport.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: How do you get to the airport? Is there a bus?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: There's no direct bus, unfortunately. You have to take a taxi — it's about 15 minutes and 1,500 tenge.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Good to know! I'm planning to fly home for the New Year break. I'll book early.

vocab.definition: a system for moving people or goods from one place to another
vocab.example: Kazakhstan's transport system is vast and diverse.

vocab.definition: the price you pay to travel on public transport
vocab.example: A bus fare in Uralsk costs around 80–100 tenge.

vocab.definition: the path you travel from one place to another
vocab.example: The number 14 bus route goes past the university.

vocab.definition: the time or act of leaving a place
vocab.example: Check the departure time before going to the station.

vocab.definition: the time or act of reaching a place
vocab.example: The train's arrival is scheduled for 6:15 pm.

vocab.definition: a raised surface at a train or bus station where you board
vocab.example: The Almaty train departs from platform 3.

vocab.definition: a plan that lists times of buses, trains, or activities
vocab.example: Always check the bus schedule before you travel.

vocab.definition: a small enclosed space in a train carriage, usually with 4 seats
vocab.example: We booked a 4-person compartment on the overnight train.

vocab.definition: a raised bank or road along a river
vocab.example: Students cycle along the river embankment on weekends.

vocab.definition: cheap enough for ordinary people to buy or use
vocab.example: The metro is fast, clean, and very affordable.

grammarNote: ИМПЕРАТИВ — это команда или указание. Используется для указания направления (turn left!), просьб (take the bus!) и советов (book early!). Он образуется из базовой формы глагола БЕЗ подлежащего. Отрицательный императив: Don't + base verb.

grammarTable.subject: Affirmative
grammarTable.example: Turn left! · Go straight! · Take the bus! · Cross the road!

grammarTable.subject: Negative
grammarTable.example: Don't turn right! · Don't miss the stop! · Don't be late!

grammarTable.subject: Polite
grammarTable.example: Please show me your ticket. · Please get off here.

grammarTable.subject: Let's
grammarTable.example: Let's take the metro! · Let's walk — it's not far.
